title: Still driving
stem:
You are an F2 doctor in a GP practice. Mr Harris, 38, has epilepsy and had a seizure two weeks ago. He tells you he is still driving to work because he'd lose his job otherwise.

He says he won't tell the DVLA.
instruction: Rank in order the following actions in response to this situation (1 = Most appropriate; 4 = Least appropriate).

options.text: Respect his confidentiality and take no further action.
options.brief: Puts him and others at serious risk.
options.detailed: Confidentiality is important, but not when someone is driving with uncontrolled epilepsy and putting others at risk.

options.text: Explain that you'd have to inform the DVLA yourself if he keeps driving, telling him first.
options.brief: Honest about what you'd need to do.
options.detailed: GMC guidance says that if a patient continues to drive against advice, you should inform the DVLA, telling the patient before you do. Being honest about this now is fair.

options.text: Discuss the situation with your GP supervisor.
options.brief: Advice helps with a difficult confidentiality decision.
options.detailed: Your supervisor can advise and support you. It ranks third because explaining to Mr Harris comes first.

options.text: Explain that he must stop driving and tell the DVLA, and why.
options.brief: He may not understand the legal and safety implications.
options.detailed: After a seizure, he must stop driving and inform the DVLA. Explaining the risks to himself and others, and the law, may persuade him.

explanation.issue: This tests how you balance confidentiality against public safety when a patient continues to drive against medical advice.
explanation.keyDetails: He has had a recent seizure. He is still driving. He refuses to tell the DVLA.
explanation.reasoning: [D] explains his duty, [B] is honest about yours, and [C] gets advice. [A] puts others at risk.
explanation.competing: This is hard because the order of [D] and [B] may feel close. The key starts with persuasion, as the GMC expects you to try to persuade him first.

references.title: Assessing fitness to drive: a guide for medical professionals
Confidentiality: good practice in handling patient information
references.note: Disclosing information to the DVLA when a patient continues to drive.
